# Intake column guide

<!-- Generated by `python manage.py export_intake_templates`. Do not edit by hand: the columns are read from the models, and a manual edit will be reverted by the next run and reported by tests/rf_confirmation. -->

One section per sheet in `templates/`. The CSV files carry a single header row so the S15 importer can read them directly; everything a person needs in order to fill one in is here.

**Leave a cell empty when the answer is unconfirmed.** An empty cell is a recorded gap. A guessed value is indistinguishable from a confirmed one the moment it is loaded, which is what acceptance criterion §26.20 exists to prevent.

## Bands — `templates/01-bands.csv`

**Answers:** OQ-14, OQ-31

Band identity is administrative, but two of its attributes are not. Which polarization types are actually in use is OQ-14, and whether modems tune on a raster is OQ-31 — without which Auto-place will propose centre frequencies no modem can be configured to.

| Column | Value | Required | Permitted values | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | text, up to 50 characters | yes | — | — |
| `name` | text, up to 200 characters | yes | — | — |
| `rf_min_hz` | Hz, whole number | yes | — | Informative lower bound, in Hz. |
| `rf_max_hz` | Hz, whole number | yes | — | Informative upper bound, in Hz. |
| `allowed_polarizations` | text | no | — | OQ-14. Semicolon-separated, from the permitted values of the polarization columns on the other sheets. Leave blank if unconfirmed — no Band ships with any preselected. |
| `tuning_raster_hz` | Hz, whole number | no | — | Minimum centre-frequency step, in Hz. Leave empty when unconfirmed (OQ-31). |
| `default_display_unit` | text, up to 20 characters | no | — | — |
| `description` | free text | no | — | — |

## Frequency Windows — `templates/02-frequency-windows.csv`

**Answers:** OQ-01, OQ-07, OQ-34

The authoritative grant of permission to allocate spectrum. Band limits are informative (§13.2); an allocation must fit inside a Window. One row is one leg of one satellite at one polarization — two polarizations on the same leg are two rows, because §25 makes them separable only as separate Windows.

| Column | Value | Required | Permitted values | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `satellite_code` | code of an existing satellite | yes | — | — |
| `band_code` | code of an existing band | yes | — | — |
| `code` | text, up to 50 characters | yes | — | — |
| `name` | text, up to 200 characters | yes | — | — |
| `side` | one of the permitted values | yes | `HUB_UPLINK, REMOTE_DOWNLINK, REMOTE_UPLINK, HUB_DOWNLINK` | Which leg of the payload chain this window covers. |
| `polarization` | one of the permitted values | yes | `RHCP, LHCP, H, V` | — |
| `rf_start_hz` | Hz, whole number | yes | — | Inclusive lower edge. Ranges are half-open, [start, end). |
| `rf_end_hz` | Hz, whole number | yes | — | Exclusive upper edge. A window ending at 14500000000 does not include that Hz; a neighbour may start there (A-11). |
| `min_edge_guard_hz` | Hz, whole number | no | — | OQ-34. Leave blank for none — blank means zero, not unknown. |
| `default_guard_policy_code` | code of an existing guard policy | no | — | From sheet 05. Leave blank if the Window has no default. |
| `effective_from` | ISO 8601 UTC, for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z | yes | — | — |
| `effective_until` | ISO 8601 UTC, for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z | no | — | Leave empty for an open-ended record. |
| `source_reference` | free text | no | — | Where this figure came from. Not ceremony — see the README. |
| `description` | free text | no | — | — |

## Payload translations — `templates/03-payload-translations.csv`

**Answers:** OQ-02

How the satellite maps an uplink frequency to its downlink frequency. §13.7 requires the mapping to be deterministic, which is why the method and constant are collected rather than inferred from the two windows' edges: any two windows sit at some offset from each other, and reading the relationship off them would produce a plausible number that is not the payload's actual translation.

| Column | Value | Required | Permitted values | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `satellite_code` | code of an existing satellite | yes | — | — |
| `code` | text, up to 50 characters | yes | — | — |
| `name` | text, up to 200 characters | yes | — | — |
| `direction` | one of the permitted values | yes | `FWD, RTN` | — |
| `uplink_window_code` | code of an existing frequency window | yes | — | From sheet 02, on the same Satellite. |
| `downlink_window_code` | code of an existing frequency window | yes | — | From sheet 02, on the same Satellite. |
| `translation_method` | one of the permitted values | yes | `OFFSET_ADD, OFFSET_SUBTRACT, LO_REFLECT` | — |
| `translation_constant_hz` | Hz, whole number | yes | — | The offset for OFFSET_ADD and OFFSET_SUBTRACT; the reflection constant K for LO_REFLECT, where downlink = K - uplink. |
| `spectral_inversion` | true or false | no | — | LO_REFLECT inverts by construction and needs no flag here. Set this only for a path that inverts for some other reason. |
| `effective_from` | ISO 8601 UTC, for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z | yes | — | — |
| `effective_until` | ISO 8601 UTC, for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z | no | — | Leave empty for an open-ended record. |
| `engineering_reference` | free text | no | — | — |
| `description` | free text | no | — | — |

**Not collected, and deliberately so:**

- `uplink_window_side` — Denormalised from the uplink Window so a composite foreign key can prove it matches the direction. Written by the import, never entered — a typed value could disagree with the Window it came from.
- `downlink_window_side` — As above, from the downlink Window.

## Polarization mappings — `templates/04-polarization-mappings.csv`

**Answers:** OQ-03

Which uplink/downlink polarization pairs each Payload Path permits. The table ships empty: a plausible default — RHCP up, RHCP down — would be indistinguishable from a confirmed one once loaded.

| Column | Value | Required | Permitted values | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `satellite_code` | text | no | — | Context. A Payload Path code is only unique within its Satellite. |
| `payload_path_code` | code of an existing payload path | yes | — | From sheet 03. |
| `uplink_polarization` | one of the permitted values | yes | `RHCP, LHCP, H, V` | — |
| `downlink_polarization` | one of the permitted values | yes | `RHCP, LHCP, H, V` | — |

## Guard policies — `templates/05-guard-policies.csv`

**Answers:** OQ-07

The separation applied either side of a transmission, by Band, Window and platform. Required separation must be expressed as a guard and never as an implicit gap: half-open ranges make touching allocations legal (A-11).

| Column | Value | Required | Permitted values | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | text, up to 50 characters | yes | — | — |
| `name` | text, up to 200 characters | yes | — | — |
| `mode` | one of the permitted values | yes | `FIXED, PERCENT_OF_OCCUPIED, MAX_OF_FIXED_AND_PERCENT` | The mode decides which of the four value columns are required. A policy missing the values its own mode needs is refused by the database rather than resolving to a zero guard. |
| `fixed_left_hz` | Hz, whole number | no | — | — |
| `fixed_right_hz` | Hz, whole number | no | — | — |
| `percent_left` | percent, up to 3 decimal places | no | — | — |
| `percent_right` | percent, up to 3 decimal places | no | — | — |
| `description` | free text | no | — | — |

## Spectrum resources — `templates/06-spectrum-resources.csv`

**Answers:** OQ-25

What competes with what. The overlap guarantee is judged on these rows: two allocations conflict when they occupy the same resource with overlapping RF and overlapping time, and nothing else about them matters. A leg mapped to no resource competes with nothing, so this sheet is the difference between a platform that prevents interference and one that merely records it.

| Column | Value | Required | Permitted values | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `satellite_code` | code of an existing satellite | yes | — | — |
| `code` | text, up to 50 characters | yes | — | — |
| `name` | text, up to 200 characters | yes | — | — |
| `kind` | one of the permitted values | yes | `PAYLOAD_INPUT, RF_CHAIN, BEAM_PLAN` | What kind of thing is shared. Recorded from the approved plan, not inferred. |
| `leg` | one of the permitted values | yes | `HUB_UPLINK, REMOTE_DOWNLINK, REMOTE_UPLINK, HUB_DOWNLINK` | Which leg of the payload chain this resource sits on. |
| `polarization` | one of the permitted values | no | `RHCP, LHCP, H, V` | Leave blank when both polarizations share the RF chain and therefore compete. Set it only where the chains are independently implemented. |
| `effective_from` | ISO 8601 UTC, for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z | yes | — | — |
| `effective_until` | ISO 8601 UTC, for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z | no | — | Leave blank for a fixed payload. A software-defined payload's resources are time-bounded, so this is where a reconfiguration is recorded. |
| `source_reference` | free text | no | — | The approved frequency and polarization plan this resource comes from. |
| `description` | free text | no | — | — |

## Equipment profiles — `templates/07-equipment-profiles.csv`

**Answers:** OQ-04, OQ-26

BUC, BDC and LNB conversion limits by site and model. These decide both the L-band IF the platform reports and which profiles it will accept for a given RF, so an approximate LO produces a confidently wrong IF.

| Column | Value | Required | Permitted values | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | text, up to 50 characters | yes | — | — |
| `name` | text, up to 200 characters | yes | — | — |
| `type` | one of the permitted values | yes | `BUC, BDC, LNB, OTHER` | — |
| `band_code` | code of an existing band | yes | — | From sheet 01. |
| `vendor` | text, up to 200 characters | no | — | — |
| `model` | text, up to 200 characters | no | — | — |
| `rf_min_hz` | Hz, whole number | yes | — | — |
| `rf_max_hz` | Hz, whole number | yes | — | — |
| `if_min_hz` | Hz, whole number | yes | — | — |
| `if_max_hz` | Hz, whole number | yes | — | — |
| `lo_hz` | Hz, whole number | yes | — | Local oscillator frequency, in Hz. |
| `conversion_method` | one of the permitted values | yes | `LO_PLUS_IF, LO_MINUS_IF, FIXED_OFFSET` | — |
| `sideband` | one of the permitted values | yes | `LOW_SIDE, HIGH_SIDE` | Must agree with the method: LO_PLUS_IF is low-side, LO_MINUS_IF is high-side. The pairing is what makes IF = \|RF - LO\| invertible, so the database enforces it. |
| `spectral_inversion` | true or false | no | — | — |
| `priority` | whole number | no | — | Lower sorts first when several profiles are valid. Blank means 100. |
| `label` | text, up to 50 characters | no | — | LOW, MID and HIGH may be used here as labels. They must never drive branching logic (§13.5), and nothing in the platform reads this field. |
| `gateway_code` | code of an existing gateway | no | — | Leave blank when the profile applies everywhere. |
| `hub_code` | code of an existing hub | no | — | Leave blank when it applies to every Hub. |
| `effective_from` | ISO 8601 UTC, for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z | yes | — | — |
| `effective_until` | ISO 8601 UTC, for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z | no | — | Leave empty for an open-ended record. |
| `engineering_reference` | free text | no | — | — |
| `description` | free text | no | — | — |
